Article Title: India, 163 others vote at UNGA for map with bigger Africa, shrunk North America
Article Text:

Poll Vote & Share your view Do you support the adoption of the new Equal Earth map by the United Nations General Assembly? Yes No Unsure 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

United Nations General Assembly voted Friday to adopt a new world map that makes the African continent bigger while shrinking North America and Europe, drawing ire from Washington.Aimed at "a more accurate representation" of continental landmasses, the resolution was supported by 164 countries, including India. US voted against it and six nations abstained.The new map, known as the Equal Earth cartographic projection, improves "the accuracy of the cartographic representation of the world", the resolution said. It urges member states to use the new map in place of the traditional Mercator projection.Foreign minister Robert Dussey of Togo, which sponsored the resolution, said maps "guide education, nourish imagination, and influence collective perceptions"."They are therefore never neutral; when they present a distorted image of our planet, they risk perpetuating inaccurate representation that is passed down through generations," he said.African Union Commission chair Mahmoud Ali Youssouf said, "Beyond cartography, this initiative underscores the importance of representing Africa on the basis of objective and scientifically established realities...Africa must be represented as it truly is: in its true dimensions and in its rightful place in the world."US, however, slammed the resolution, saying such moves are "the reason this institution is losing its credibility". Representative Yaryna Ferencevych said, "Instead of focusing on genuine problems... this body is debating map projects from the 16th century and their role in promoting reparations and cognitive justice."The Mercator projection was designed for maritime navigation by Flemish cartographer Gerardus Mercator in 1569. It focused on depictions of the shapes and angles of land masses but their relative sizes were often inaccurate, largely due to the challenge of rendering a three-dimensional globe onto a two-dimensional map.It inflated northern regions and compressed equatorial ones, making Europe and North America appear much larger, while shrinking Africa and South America. Africa appears to be roughly as big as Greenland, though at 30.3 million sq km, it's about 14 times as large.France, which co-sponsored the resolution, announced Friday it would abandon the Mercator projection, in which "US, Russia and China take on a disproportionate visual prominence". Foreign minister Jean-Noel Barrot said, "Changing maps obviously doesn't change the world," "But correcting a distorted representation is already an act of truth."
Article Summary: The united nations general assembly voted friday to adopt a new world map that makes the african continent bigger. The resolution was supported by 164 countries, including india. Us voted against it and six nations abstained. The new map, known as the equal earth cartographic projection, improves "the accuracy of the cartographic representation of the world"

NEW DELHI: After endorsing a UN General Assembly resolution on equal-area world map, the govt warned Sunday that the proposed new map must depict India's sovereign territory, including the Union territories of Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh, in accordance with India's official map and any inaccurate or misleading depiction would be unacceptable."Our position on India's sovereignty and territorial integrity is clear, consistent and non-negotiable," said MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal, replying to media queries.India was among the 164 countries that voted in favour of UN General Assembly's Sept 4 resolution, "Correct the Map: Rebalancing Global Cartographic Representation and Promoting Equitable Representation of the World's Regions, Particularly Africa".MEA said the resolution's purpose is to encourage the use of equal-area map projections that preserve the relative sizes of continental landmasses, and it neither adopts nor authenticates any particular world map, nor does it address political cartography, including international boundaries, disputed territories or place names."India voted in favour of the resolution and also made an explanation, stressing the underlying principle of promoting equal-area cartographic representation.We also highlighted that the resolution does not constitute endorsement of any specific map, projection or depiction of national boundaries," said Randhir Jaiswal.The resolution received abstentions from Estonia, Georgia, Lithuania, Moldova, Serbia and Ukraine, and a lone vote against it from US.The resolution noted that the Mercator projection remains widely used in educational, media, digital and official materials, despite the considerable distortion of landmasses to the North and South, far from the equator.It expressed concern that this distortion contributed to minimising the perceived sizes of Africa, Latin America and South Asia, and perpetuating an unbalanced view of the world. India welcomed the intention behind the resolution to promote more accurate and representative cartographic practices.

Article Title: 'Contributed to population control': Former CEC Quraishi says EC 'eliminated' 15 cr voters through SIR
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Former Chief Election Commissioner SY Quraishi on Sunday criticised the Election Commission over its special intensive revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, claiming that the exercise had effectively removed around 14-15 crore people from the country's voter lists.Speaking to news agency ANI, Quraishi urged the poll panel to disclose the number of voters deleted, describing the exercise as a "great success" in achieving something the National Population Commission could not."I would like to compliment the Election Commission for completing a very difficult mission of eliminating about 14-15 crore population of India through this exercise. I don't know how many illegal immigrants they have found, which was the main purpose of this exercise. It's a pity they have not disclosed this figure," Quraishi said."I would request them to please come out with this figure, so that we know what a great success you have been, and also that you have achieved something that the National Population Commission could not do. You have contributed a lot to population control by eliminating about 15% of India's population," he added.Quraishi also questioned the intent behind the SIR exercise, arguing that voting is a constitutional right and not something to be granted by the Election Commission."I think the entire SIR exercise is not well-intentioned. The way it has deleted crores of voters is tinkering with democracy. You are a citizen of India. I'm a citizen of India. Voting is our constitutional right," he said."Article 326 says that everyone shall be registered. So it is not a charity from the Election Commission that they will give you that," he added.The Election Commission is conducting the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls in several states to ensure that voter lists are accurate, updated and free of ineligible or duplicate entries, while ensuring that no eligible voter is left out.The nationwide SIR was announced in October 2025 by Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. The poll panel cited migration, voters being registered at multiple places, failure to remove deceased voters and the inclusion of foreign nationals in electoral rolls as factors behind the exercise.The revision has since been rolled out across several states and Union territories, including those heading into elections. The exercise has drawn sustained criticism from opposition parties.In Maharashtra, the SIR came under scrutiny after the draft electoral roll showed around two crore fewer voters than the previous roll.According to data released by Maharashtra's Chief Electoral Officer, 7,71,65,562 of the state's 9,78,54,049 electors had submitted their enumeration forms as of August 17.
Article Summary: Former chief election commissioner sy quraishi criticised the election commission over its special intensive revision (sir) of electoral rolls. He claimed that the exercise had effectively removed around 14-15 crore people from the country's voter lists.

Article Title: India supplied 60% of diesel to Europe in August as Russian, US supplies plunge: Report
Article Text:
India emerges as key diesel supplier to Europe

India supplied about 60 per cent of the diesel transiting through the Bab-el-Mandeb towards Europe in August, strengthening its role as a key source of refined fuel as Russian exports remain depressed and US shipments begin to decline, according to a report.Around 2,00,000 barrels per day of diesel, or gasoil, crossed the strategic shipping route for Europe last month, close to year-earlier levels after flows nearly stalled in March and April. Indian refiners accounted for roughly 60 per cent of that volume, energy analytics firm Vortexa said in a report.India, the world’s fourth-largest refiner, has 258.1 million tonnes per annum of installed capacity, above domestic fuel demand. It exported 61.5 million tonnes of petroleum products in 2025-26, making it a major global supplier, PTI reported.However, sustaining these flows could become difficult. India’s crude and condensate imports fell to about 3.8 million barrels per day in August from 4.8 million barrels per day a year earlier, data showed.Russian diesel exports averaged only around 1,50,000 barrels per day during the first 25 days of August, down about 6,10,000 barrels per day year-on-year and 81 per cent below the five-year seasonal average.The scheduled easing of Russia’s diesel export ban from September 1 may not quickly restore supplies, with Ukrainian drone strikes continuing to disrupt refineries and export infrastructure. Vortexa recorded 32 refinery attacks across July and August.The Perm refinery, with capacity of 2,60,000 barrels per day, was left operating at only about 28 per cent of its crude distillation capacity after an attack, while no diesel cargoes have left Tuapse since a May strike.The US supplied about half of Europe’s seaborne diesel imports from outside the region in August, at around 5,20,000 barrels per day. But shipments fell from nearly 5,40,000 barrels per day in the first half of August to about 3,50,000 barrels per day in the second half.
Article Summary: India supplied about 60 per cent of the diesel transiting through the bab-el-mandeb towards europe in august. India, the world’s fourth-largest refiner, has 258.1 million tonnes per annum of installed capacity, above domestic fuel demand.

Article Title: “I never thought I was going to do it”: Cole Johnson reveals how a joke suddenly turned into a real fight after a huge offer came his way
Article Text:
Cole Johnson (Image via IG/X)

Cole Johnson says a joke changed when people started offering him serious money

Fans are questioning whether Cole Johnson’s dangerous challenge should happen at all

Cole Johnson did not expect a joke about fighting a chimpanzee to become a real fight proposal. The 1-0 amateur MMA fighter, better known as Wavy MMA, says an offhand claim turned into serious money offers and a proposed pay-per-view event. Now, a reported September 11 date has put his bizarre challenge in the spotlight. The bigger question is no longer whether Johnson believes he can win. It is whether this fight should happen at all.Johnson did not begin with plans to actually fight a chimpanzee.The idea started with a video he made as a joke. But the reaction online quickly changed things when people began reaching out to him with serious offers.Johnson said one person offered him $500,000 to take part in a fight involving a chimpanzee in an unnamed country. He eventually agreed to explore the opportunity, but the arrangement fell apart after he decided the person behind it could not be trusted.That could have been the end of it.Instead, Johnson claims another offer came along for even more money. He has not revealed the amount, but says the people behind the new proposal appeared more trustworthy.A promotional website for the event has since appeared online, with a reported September 11 date.The location has not been publicly revealed.The attention surrounding the proposed matchup has also pushed Johnson to explain how he believes such a confrontation could work.He says the chimpanzee would not have its teeth or claws removed. He has also claimed that people with tranquilizers would be nearby in case the situation became too dangerous.Johnson has made it clear that he knows there is a serious risk involved.“I don’t want to kill this wild animal and I don’t want to die,” he said while discussing the proposed fight.That admission is important because Johnson is not describing the matchup as a normal MMA contest.A human opponent understands the rules, knows when a referee can stop the fight and can choose to tap out. A chimpanzee would not understand any of those things.Johnson still believes his years of training could give him a chance.His background is built around wrestling and grappling, and he appears confident that those skills could help him control the animal if the situation allows it.But that confidence comes with a clear warning.Johnson has admitted that he could suffer a serious injury during the encounter. He has even discussed the need to protect vulnerable parts of his body because he knows the animal would not fight like a trained MMA opponent.The money may have helped turn the idea into something more serious, but Johnson's comments suggest he understands that the potential consequences could be far more important than the payday.Once news of the proposed fight spread, the reaction from fans was largely filled with concern and disbelief.Some people online questioned whether the event was even genuine. Others immediately focused on the safety issues surrounding it.The question of animal welfare has also become impossible to ignore.In a normal MMA fight, both competitors agree to participate. They train for combat, understand what is expected of them and know there are rules designed to protect them.That is why this proposed event raises questions that go far beyond whether Johnson could win.Even if organizers have medical personnel and tranquilizers nearby, stopping an animal in the middle of an aggressive encounter is not the same as stopping a human fighter.There is also no guarantee that a situation would remain under control long enough for anyone to intervene.Johnson himself has acknowledged that a serious injury is possible.“I’m not saying I’m going to come out of this thing unscathed,” he said.That statement has given fans another reason to question the entire idea.Some online reactions have been blunt, with viewers predicting severe injuries and questioning how the event could possibly be legal or ethical.Others have simply dismissed the proposed fight as something that will never happen.For now, there are still plenty of unanswered questions.The location has not been revealed, the exact rules remain unclear and there is uncertainty over what kind of oversight would actually be in place.The existence of a promotional website and a countdown does not necessarily mean the event is ready to happen as advertised.What is clear is that Johnson's original joke has grown far beyond what he expected. He reportedly never planned to take the idea seriously. Then the offers started arriving.Now, the 1-0 fighter finds himself at the center of a bizarre combat-sports story that has sparked debates about money, personal risk, animal welfare and the limits of fight entertainment.But Johnson's own words explain why the story has caught so much attention. What began as a joke became a serious proposition once someone was willing to pay him to prove whether his confidence was justified.
Article Summary: Cole johnson says a joke turned into serious money offers and a proposed pay-per-view event. A promotional website for the event has since appeared online, with a reported september 11 date. Johnson has made it clear that he knows there is a serious risk involved.

Article Text:

A celebration turned tragedy in Mexico killed at least 10 people while leaving 64 injured after pyrotechnic material exploded during a religious festival in Temascalcingo on Saturday night. The explosion collapsed walls and sent hundreds of people fleeing in panic, authorities said.The blast occurred beside the Nuestra Señora de la Luz church in the central Mexican town where residents were gathered to watch a fireworks display being held as part of celebrations for the local patron saint. The municipality is located about 160 kilometres (100 miles) northwest of Mexico City.The explosion brought down the walls of surrounding buildings and triggered a fire in the town square.Footage circulating online from the accident shows people dancing around with the firework structure in celebration. It was after a couple of rounds that the pyrotechnics began going berserk. Due to the nature of the structure, the smoke from the firework billowed rapidly in the air before the people could react to the mishap.Videos from the aftermath were also circulated online showing people moving through thick smoke and scattered debris as they searched for survivors.Some victims were reportedly trapped beneath collapsed structures.The cause of the explosion has not yet been established. The Mexico State Attorney General’s Office has opened an investigation into the incident.A local bishop said two priests were among those injured in the blast.The explosion occurred during a traditional festival ritual in which a straw bull fitted with fireworks is burned and carried around the town. Video footage showed the blast striking as crowds stood outside the church, with the force of the explosion causing widespread panic.Emergency responders and residents rushed to help those caught in the blast, as the scale of the destruction became clear in the aftermath.Temascalcingo, a municipality with about 66,000 residents, was hosting hundreds of people for the religious celebrations when the explosion occurred.The incident has once again highlighted the dangers posed by pyrotechnics in Mexico, where fireworks are widely used during street celebrations, religious festivals and other public gatherings.Similar accidents have occurred in the country before. Nearly four years ago, a powerful fireworks explosion in a village in the municipality of Huejutla, in the central state of Hidalgo, left 17 people injured.
Article Summary: The explosion occurred during a religious festival in temascalcingo, mexico. Video footage showed the blast striking as crowds stood outside the church. Some victims were reportedly trapped beneath collapsed structures. The mexico state attorney general’s office has opened an investigation.

Article Title: 'They're clearly hoping to kill him in there': Imran Khan's sons raise serious concerns
Article Text:
Imran Khan (Image credit: X)

‘They're clearly hoping to kill him in there’

‘They made absolute fools of themselves’

Authorities deny mistreatment claims

The sons of former Pakistan captain and Prime Minister Imran Khan have strongly criticised Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB) chairman Mohsin Naqvi after the board was accused of threatening to abandon the Lord’s Test against England. Sulaiman and Kasim Khan also raised serious concerns about their father's health and conditions in prison, claiming that Pakistan authorities are trying to silence him.The controversy began during the second Test at Lord’s after Sky Sports aired an interview conducted by former England captain Michael Atherton with Sulaiman and Kasim.They spoke about their father's health and his conditions in prison.Reports later claimed that the PCB threatened not to send the Pakistan team out for the post-lunch session on the first day unless the interview was taken off air.With Mohsin Naqvi facing increased scrutiny, the sons also spoke about their concerns over Khan's solitary confinement.Kasim made a serious allegation about the former Pakistan captain's safety.“They're clearly hoping to kill him in there. They want to silence him as secretly as possible and just slowly make him fade into nothing.“That's a very difficult thing to do with the most popular person in Pakistan right now.Their strategy, whenever we speak, is to let everything fizzle out and then impose more brutal restrictions that make it even harder for him to survive.”Kasim criticised the PCB's reported reaction and said the board had damaged its own image.“They made absolute fools of themselves,” Kasim told The Telegraph on Sunday.Sulaiman said he was surprised that the PCB reacted so strongly to an interview about his father.“I was expecting some sort of response. But I didn't think they would be so tactless as to threaten not to take to the field.“It shouldn't be in the remit of the Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB) to ask for an interview about an ex-Pakistan player, somebody who lived in England for 22 years, to be taken down. This wasn't about politics, but about the humanitarian situation and his health.”Pakistani authorities have repeatedly denied allegations of mistreatment and have maintained that Khan is receiving proper medical care.Sulaiman, however, questioned those assurances and said the family had not been given enough information about his father's condition.“The worrying theory we're hearing is that they're drip-feeding these reports of his ailing health and pretending that they're trying to help him, just to lay the ground for something worse to happen. Then they can wash their hands and say: 'He's just an old man who died, and we had nothing to do with it.’“They haven't given us proof of any of this. It's all just hearsay from government sources – there's no transparency, they don't want to give anyone access, so how are we supposed to believe any of it? The last verifiable piece of information we had was from him, six months ago, when he spoke about his eye and how it had been neglected.”
Article Summary: Sulaiman and kasim khan spoke to michael atherton about their father's health and conditions in prison. They claim pakistan authorities are trying to silence imran khan. Reports claim the pcb threatened not to send the pakistan team out for the post-lunch session on the first day unless the interview was taken off air.

Article Title: Video captures moment Amazon cargo plane hurtles off runway, erupts in flames
Article Text:
Five people were killed in the crash, while another five were injured

Huge emergency response as flights disrupted

An Amazon Prime Air cargo plane overran the runway at Miami International Airport on Sunday afternoon, striking multiple vehicles and bursting into flames in a deadly crash that killed at least five people and injured five others.The Boeing 767-300, operating as Amazon Prime Air Flight 7598 and operated by cargo carrier 21 Air, had arrived from San Juan, Puerto Rico, when the aircraft ran off the runway shortly before 2pm local time.Dramatic footage showed the plane racing beyond the runway before crashing through an area used by warehouse workers and other businesses surrounding the airport. Thick black smoke and flames could be seen rising from the aircraft as emergency crews rushed to the scene.The plane eventually came to rest beside a roadway near two semi-trucks. Images showed the aircraft largely intact but resting on its belly and engulfed in flames.Five people were killed in the crash, while another five were injured. Three of the injured were in critical condition, according to Miami-Dade County officials. It was initially unclear whether the pilots survived or whether all those killed were in vehicles struck by the aircraft.Miami-Dade Fire Rescue Chief Ray Jadallah said the pilot and co-pilot were trapped inside the cockpit following the crash, while some people were also trapped in vehicles. Crews had to rescue a person who was pinned beneath a vehicle.More than 60 Miami-Dade Fire Rescue units and around 200 emergency personnel responded as firefighters battled an intense fire involving the aircraft. Specialised airport firefighting units used foam to extinguish the flames, while crews continued dealing with a fuel leak several hours after the crash.The accident brought operations at the busy airport to a halt for much of Sunday afternoon, with more than 160 flights cancelled and nearly 325 delayed by late in the day. Some flights were also diverted to Orlando International Airport.The cause of the crash remains unknown and is being investigated by the Federal Aviation Administration and National Transportation Safety Board, which sent a team led by its chairwoman, Jennifer Homendy, to Miami.Weather conditions may also form part of the investigation, with thunderstorms and wind gusts of up to 30 mph recorded in the area around the time of the crash.Aviation experts have raised questions about the aircraft's landing. Former United Airlines pilot Steve Arroyo said investigators would need to establish whether the plane touched down within the designated landing zone and, if not, why the crew did not abort the landing and attempt another approach.Former Transportation Department inspector general Mary Schiavo, meanwhile, said video of the landing appeared to show the aircraft floating above the runway for an extended period before touching down, potentially leaving insufficient runway to stop safely.
Article Summary: Five people were killed in the crash, while another five were injured. The boeing 767-300 was operating as amazon prime air flight 7598. It had arrived from san juan, puerto rico, when the aircraft ran off the runway. The cause of the crash remains unknown and is being investigated.

Article Title: Suspected drones near Amritsar airport trigger flight diversions, security alert
Article Text:
Airport operations remained suspended from 9.50 pm to 11.15 pm, he said. (File Photo)





AMRITSAR: Suspected drone-like objects were reportedly spotted near Sri Guru Ram Das Ji International Airport late on Sunday night, triggering a major security alert and leading to the diversion of seven incoming flights as a precautionary measure.Anirudh Sharma, who holds the additional charge of Airport Director, confirmed that drone-like objects were noticed in the vicinity of the airport. Following the alert, two incoming flights were diverted to Chandigarh and five to Delhi. Airport operations remained suspended from 9.50 pm to 11.15 pm, he said.Sources said the suspected flying objects were seen outside the airport's perimeter wall, following which Air Traffic Control (ATC) suspended landing operations due to concerns over the safety of aircraft operating in the area.Sources said the police suspect that the drones were flown locally.The incident is being viewed seriously, particularly because the international airport is located close to the India-Pakistan border. Security agencies were immediately alerted, while the matter was also reported to the police for investigation.Sources said the Central Industrial Security Force (CISF), responsible for airport security, has also heightened its vigilance following the incidentWhile the exact nature and origin of the suspected objects are yet to be established, investigators are examining all possibilities.Sources did not rule out the possibility that locally operated drones may have entered the restricted airspace near the airport.However, given the increasing instances of drones allegedly being used from across the Pakistan border to smuggle narcotics, arms and ammunition into Punjab, security agencies are also examining whether there could be a cross-border angle, sources said.Sharma said the matter had been reported to the police, who are now investigating the incident to determine whether the suspicious flying objects were actually drones or some other objects and where they were flown from.
Article Summary: Two incoming flights were diverted to chandigarh and five to delhi. Airport operations remained suspended from 9.50 pm to 11.15 pm. Police suspect that the drones were flown locally. Incident is being viewed seriously because the international airport is located close to the india-pakistan border.

Article Title: RAKSHA Document : India unveils 10-year ‘RAKSHA’ roadmap to expand global defence & security ties

India looks to expand strategic defence ties under new ‘RAKSHA’ framework

Four key pillars of India's defence diplomacy roadmap

Strategic partnerships: Deepening bilateral and multilateral security cooperation.

Capacity building: Expanding joint military exercises, training programmes and the sharing of best practices with friendly nations.

Indigenous exports: Promoting Make-in-India defence platforms to position India as a reliable global defence manufacturing hub .

Senior officials attend release event

Rajnath Singh calls for stronger India-Belgium cooperation

Defence minister Rajnath Singh on Thursday released the ‘RAKSHA’ document on defence diplomacy, outlining India's strategic roadmap and vision for expanding global defence partnerships over the next 10 years.The document, unveiled at a special event in New Delhi, lays out a framework aimed at aligning India's national security objectives with proactive international cooperation, according to the ministry of defence.The strategic blueprint focuses on deepening bilateral and multilateral security ties, building capacity with friendly countries, promoting indigenous defence exports and strengthening maritime security.The ‘RAKSHA’ framework is built around four key pillars:The ministry of defence said the document provides a “clear, actionable vision” for the next decade as defence diplomacy remains a core pillar of India's foreign policy.The framework is aimed at ensuring India remains an anchor of peace, stability and a rules-based order in an evolving global landscape.Chief of the Army Staff General Dhiraj Seth, defence secretary Rajesh Kumar Singh and secretary (defence production) Sanjeev Kumar were among the senior officials present at the event.Secretary (east) in the ministry of external affairs Rudrendra Tandon, Vice Chief of the Air Staff Air Marshal Ashutosh Dixit and Vice Chief of the Naval Staff Vice Admiral Ajay Kochhar also attended.The document was officially released during an event at Kartavya Bhawan.The directorate of public relations, ministry of defence, said in a post on X that the framework sets a 10-year roadmap to strengthen global security partnerships.“Aligning national security with proactive international cooperation, this comprehensive framework aims to position India as a key defence manufacturing hub and an anchor of regional stability,” it added.The document also seeks to strengthen India's role as a Net Security Provider and First Responder in the Indian Ocean Region, with defence diplomacy described as a core pillar of the country's foreign policy.The release came a day after India and Belgium held extensive discussions aimed at expanding bilateral defence and industrial cooperation.Singh hosted Belgian defence and trade minister Theo Francken in New Delhi on Wednesday, with multiple memorandums of understanding and contracts signed under defence industrial cooperation.“Had a very productive meeting with the Defence and Trade Minister of Belgium, Mr @FranckenTheo, in New Delhi today. We reviewed the entire spectrum of Defence relations and Defence Industrial Cooperation between India and Belgium. Multiple MoUs and contracts under the Defence Industrial Cooperation were also signed, towards leveraging Belgian technology together with Indian skill and scale,” Singh said.On Thursday, Singh called for greater cooperation between the two countries during the India-Belgium Ministers' Meeting in the national capital.“The world is witnessing a time of great geopolitical and economic turmoil. Most of it is not our doing, but we have to handle the challenges. In such situations, meeting a friend and partner like you provides a useful opportunity to exchange views and perspectives,” he said.Singh said the recently held India-Belgium Strategic Dialogue had provided a framework for taking the bilateral partnership forward, including in defence and security.
Article Summary: India looks to expand strategic defence ties under new ‘raksha’ framework. Four key pillars of india's defence diplomacy roadmap are:strategic partnerships: deepening bilateral and multilateral security cooperation. Capacity building: expanding joint military exercises, training programmes and the sharing of best practices with friendly nations.

Article Title: Amazon cargo plane crashes at Miami International Airport, kills 5: Here’s the latest update shared by the company
Article Text:
Amazon cargo crash

Amazon plane crash at Miami airport

Here’s the update shared by Amazon

Updated at 3:05 p.m. PT

"We're heartbroken to learn that five people lost their lives in today’s incident at Miami International Airport.

Our deepest sympathies go out to the families, loved ones, and all those affected by this devastating loss.

The airplane, which was operated by 21 Air, was attempting to land when this incident occurred. We're working closely with local authorities and officials to learn more and will cooperate fully with any investigation." — Kelly Nantel, Amazon spokesperson

1:58 p.m. PT

"We can confirm that an Amazon Air plane operated by 21 Air experienced an incident while attempting to land at Miami International Airport today. This is a fast-moving situation and we're still gathering details. We're working closely with local authorities and officials to understand exactly what happened. Right now, our absolute priority is the safety, well-being, and care of everyone involved. We're doing everything we can to support those affected.

" — Kelly Nantel, Amazon spokesperson

An Amazon cargo aircraft operated by 21 Air crashed while attempting to land at Miami International Airport on September 6, killing at least five people and injuring five others. The aircraft overran the runway and struck several vehicles before catching fire, according to local officials.vAmazon confirmed that the aircraft was an Amazon Air plane operated by 21 Air and said it was working with local authorities to understand what happened. In a latest update, the company said its priority was the safety and care of those affected by the crash.“We're heartbroken to learn that five people lost their lives in today’s incident at Miami International Airport. Our deepest sympathies go out to the families, loved ones, and all those affected by this devastating loss,” Amazon spokesperson Kelly Nantel said in a statement shared on Amazon News website.The Boeing 767 was attempting to land when it left the usable portion of the runway and hit multiple vehicles. The crash caused a large fire, with thick black smoke visible above the airport.Miami-Dade Fire Rescue Chief Raied “Ray” Jadallah said five people were killed and another five were injured.Three of the injured were in critical condition and were taken to a trauma centre. Two others were taken to a local hospital. Several people were trapped inside vehicles struck by the aircraft and had to be removed by emergency crews.According to Miami-Dade Fire Rescue, more than 60 emergency units responded to the crash.“21 Air Flight 7598 overran the runway after landing at Miami International Airport around 2 p.m. local time on Sunday, Sept. 6. The Boeing 767-300 cargo aircraft departed from Luis Muñoz Marín International Airport in San Juan, Puerto Rico. The FAA will investigate. Contact the airline for additional information,” the Federal Aviation Administration shared in a post on X.
Article Summary: The boeing 767 was attempting to land when it left the usable portion of the runway and hit multiple vehicles. Amazon confirmed that the aircraft was an amazon air plane operated by 21 air and said it was working with local authorities to understand what happened. Several people were trapped inside vehicles struck by the aircraft.
